app.name: CO₂ Absorption Calculator
app.tagline: How much carbon does your landscape breathe in?

settings.title: Settings
settings.copernicusLead: Satellite imagery is processed on the Copernicus openEO service with your free account. Paste an OAuth client below — it is verified, then stored only on this server.
settings.sourceEnv: Managed by the server .env file — edit it there.
settings.confirmRemove: Remove the stored Copernicus credentials? New calculations will fail until you add them again.
steps: Log in to the Copernicus dashboard with your account.
Open your account menu (top right) → User settings.
Under OAuth clients, click + Create, give it a name and choose “Never” as expiry.
Copy the Client ID and the Client secret — the secret is shown only once.
settings.security: The secret is never shown again, sent back to the browser or written to logs. It is stored in the server's data folder, readable only by the app's user.
settings.localOnly: For safety, settings can only be changed from the computer running the app, or with a demo password configured (DEMO_PASSWORD).
settings.noAccount: No account? Register for free at dataspace.copernicus.eu.

home.lead: Draw any region on the map, pick a month and let Sentinel-2 imagery, ESA WorldCover land cover and NASA POWER climate data estimate how much CO₂ its plants absorbed — and how that compares with local emissions.
home.emptyBody: Create your first region to start measuring.
steps: Outline a municipality, park or farm — up to {{max}} km².
Pick one month or a whole year; each month is processed in the background.
Explore NDVI, productivity and CO₂ maps, compare months and export reports.

newRegion.name: Region name
newRegion.drawFirst: Draw or upload a region first

about.title: The method
about.lead: Net primary productivity (NPP) — the carbon plants fix through photosynthesis minus what they respire — is estimated with the CASA light-use-efficiency model, then converted to CO₂.
about.formula: NPP = 0.5 · SOL · FPAR · T1 · T2 · WSC · Eₘₐₓ
terms: Monthly incoming solar radiation (MJ/m²) from NASA POWER; half of it is photosynthetically active.
Fraction of that light absorbed by the canopy, scaled linearly from Sentinel-2 NDVI (B04, B08) between the CASA references 0.023 and 0.70 (Zhu et al., 2006).
Temperature stress factors from monthly air temperature and the optimal temperature (warmest month).
Water stress from the Shortwave Infrared Moisture Index (Sentinel-2 B11, B12), normalised within the region (Fensholt & Sandholt, 2003), between 0.5 and 1.
Maximum light-use efficiency for each ESA WorldCover 2021 land-cover class.
about.origin: This web app rebuilds the final-year project (PFC) developed at ISEL for the municipality of Oeiras. The thesis reports, posters and the original reference run (June 2024) are kept for comparison.
about.limits: Results are monthly estimates. Climate inputs are coarse (~50 km) so detail comes from vegetation indices and land cover; built-up areas and water absorb nothing in this model.
